description: Card and account movements (MX, CO, AR), one row per transaction, on event time. Grounding source for dispute intake: the customer's own products and movements. Typed, normalized and checked from workspace.bronze.transactions.

load.notes: One file per calendar day (process_date, weekends included). Clustered by customer and event date for the intake lookups (a customer's recent movements); partitioning by process_date would give 1,097 partitions of ~4k rows. customers and products are joined from Bronze (broadcast) for the derived flags.

transaction_id.description: Transaction identifier (TRX- + 20 characters), trimmed and upper-cased. Primary key.

event_ts.description: Event time of the movement (Bronze transaction_date). Use it for every time-based answer, filter and split; timezone not documented (single system clock).

event_date.description: Calendar date of event_ts. The date to quote to the customer ('when did it happen').

process_date.description: Business date with a 06:00 cut-off (25.0% of rows carry the previous day) and the landing partition of the row. Partition/business key only: never for time logic or splits.

product_id.description: Product (card or account) the movement belongs to; always owned by customer_id (see product_owner_matches).

customer_id.description: Customer who owns the product and made the movement.

transaction_category.description: Spending category. Present only for Purchase and Payment (NULL = not applicable elsewhere; about 5% missing on those two types).

amount.description: Amount in the transaction currency, always positive (direction comes from transaction_type). The amount a dispute case must take.

currency.description: ISO currency of amount. Mexican customers transact in USD only (issue 11); MXN never appears here.

amount_usd.description: FIX: USD equivalent at the source's fixed rates (ARS/350, COP/4000, USD 1:1), rounded half-even to cents. The delivered value when present, otherwise computed the same way. Internal only (policy thresholds and priority); a customer-facing conversion, if one is ever added, must use daily_exchange_rates and say so (none exists today).

amount_usd_raw.description: USD equivalent as delivered: NULL for every USD row and for 5.0% of ARS/COP rows.

amount_usd_imputed.description: True when amount_usd was computed here because the source left it empty (all USD rows 1:1, plus 99,477 ARS/COP rows).

channel.description: Channel of the movement (POS and ATM upper-case, others title case).

branch_id.description: Branch for ATM and Branch channel movements (NULL = not applicable elsewhere; about 5% missing on those channels).

merchant_name.description: Merchant for purchases (NULL = not applicable for other types; about 5% missing on purchases).

merchant_category.description: Merchant category for purchases (NULL = not applicable for other types).

transaction_country.description: Country as delivered. Mexico appears with and without the accent (40,515 unaccented rows); join and compare on transaction_country_code.

transaction_country_code.description: FIX: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of transaction_country after accent folding.

transaction_city.description: City of the movement (about 10% missing); always a city of transaction_country.

customer_country_code.description: Home country of the customer (customers.country, accent-folded to ISO), joined at build time.

is_international.description: True when transaction_country_code differs from customer_country_code (202,800 rows; the unaccented 'Mexico' would add 18,412 false positives without normalization).

response_code.description: Authorization response code (string, leading zeros kept): 00 approved; 05, 14, 51, 54 are templated decline codes (about 24% each, also on Pending and Reversed rows). Explain declines from a code-to-message table, not from this field alone.

response_code_null_reason.description: Why response_code is NULL: not_applicable = Approved (no decline to explain; 00 implied), missing = Declined, Pending or Reversed without a code (insufficient-data path). NULL when a code is present.

is_fraud.description: Fraud label (0.0975%). Flat along every observable dimension (temporal AUC 0.504): not learnable, never a training target.

fraud_score.description: Score built from is_fraud (non-fraud never exceeds 30; precision 1.000 above 30). Label-derived: never a feature, a model input or a baseline to beat. NULL in 20% of rows.

latitude.description: Latitude in decimal degrees; NULL unless the raw point lies inside the transaction country (the point is the customer's home city, and Mexican points are placeholders near 0,0).

longitude.description: Longitude in decimal degrees; NULL under the same rule as latitude.

latitude_raw.description: Latitude as delivered (typed); present for about 28% of POS, ATM and Branch rows only.

has_valid_coordinates.description: True when both raw coordinates fall inside the transaction country's bounding box (domestic AR and CO rows only in the delivered data).

implausible_type_channel.description: FLAG: type x channel pair that cannot happen (Withdrawal via POS, Web, App or Transfer; Deposit via POS; Purchase via ATM, Transfer or Branch): 1,240,000 rows (28.0%). The generator draws channel independently of type. Omit the channel when narrating these rows.

activity_before_opening.description: FLAG: event_date is before the product's opening_date (827,610 rows, 18.7%). NULL when the product is unknown. The movement stays valid; issue 8 moves the product's effective opening date back instead.

activity_before_registration.description: FLAG: event_date is before the customer's registration_date (829,540 rows). NULL when the customer is unknown.

product_owner_matches.description: True when the product's owner (products.customer_id) is customer_id: the grounding invariant of the dispute flow (100% in Bronze). NULL when the product is unknown; FALSE rows are quarantined.

checks.name: transaction_id_format
checks.description: Identifier follows the TRX- + 20 characters pattern.

checks.name: amount_positive
checks.description: Typed amount is present and positive; a case cannot be built on a missing or non-positive amount.

checks.name: product_owned_by_customer
checks.description: The product belongs to the transaction's customer (EDA section 3 control: 4,425,008 of 4,425,008). A movement on someone else's product must never be shown to a customer.

checks.name: process_date_business_cutoff
checks.expr: process_date = event_date OR (process_date = date_sub(event_date, 1) AND date_format(event_ts, 'HH:mm') <= '06:00')
checks.description: process_date is the event date, or the previous day for events before the 06:00 cut-off (51 rows at 06:00:xx sit on the boundary); never a later day.

checks.name: event_not_in_future
checks.description: The movement did not happen in the future.

checks.name: amount_usd_fixed_rate
checks.expr: amount_usd_raw IS NULL OR abs(amount_usd_raw - amount / CASE currency WHEN 'USD' THEN 1 WHEN 'ARS' THEN 350 WHEN 'COP' THEN 4000 END) <= 0.005
checks.description: Delivered amount_usd equals amount at the fixed rate within half a cent (the source rounds in floating point, so exact ties may differ by one cent from the computed fill).

checks.name: amount_usd_delivered
checks.description: Counts ARS/COP rows whose amount_usd was filled here (FIX applied; 99,477 in Bronze).

checks.name: response_code_matches_status
checks.description: Code 00 appears exactly on Approved rows.

checks.name: response_code_present_when_expected
checks.description: Counts Declined, Pending and Reversed rows without a response code.

checks.name: merchant_only_on_purchases
checks.expr: transaction_type = 'Purchase' OR (merchant_name IS NULL AND merchant_category IS NULL)
checks.description: Merchant fields appear only on purchases.

checks.name: branch_only_on_branch_channels
checks.expr: channel IN ('ATM', 'Branch') OR branch_id IS NULL
checks.description: branch_id appears only for ATM and Branch channel movements.

checks.name: coordinates_in_country
checks.expr: latitude_raw IS NULL OR longitude_raw IS NULL OR has_valid_coordinates
checks.description: Raw coordinates fall inside the transaction country; failures are Mexican placeholders near (0, 0) and home-city points on international rows, nulled in latitude/longitude.
